title: Foundations and the learning–robustness tradeoff
question: What should remain invariant, and what should change when the target changes?

title: Self-supervised learning and representation dynamics
question: Learn useful representations, distinguish encoder and projector behavior, and measure collapse over time.

title: Architectures and multimodal fusion
question: Examine tokenization, attention, complementary information and failure under missing or dominant modalities.

title: Data and pretraining choices
question: Track how curation, duplication, compute and compromised training affect later behavior.

title: Adaptation, task heads, and interaction
question: Adapt a pretrained model under explicit data, parameter and interface constraints.

title: Human preferences and representational alignment
question: Separate preference optimization and human similarity from robustness guarantees.

title: Representation, model, and visual editing
question: Identify what is edited, how local the change should be, and which unrelated behaviors must survive.

title: Failure detection and prediction trust
question: Distinguish incorrect predictions, shifted distributions, anomalies, novelty and adversarial inputs.

title: Red teaming and runtime safeguards
question: Discover failures under reproducible conditions, then evaluate mitigation together with benign utility.

title: Explanations, introspection, and mechanistic transparency
question: Ask what supports a decision, whether an explanation is faithful, and how diagnostic features can inform decisions.

title: Uncertainty, calibration, and selective decisions
question: Separate ranking, calibrated probability, coverage and explanatory uncertainty.

title: Benchmarks and domain resources
question: Evaluate different failure families and domains with their original protocols.

title: Feedback, continual learning, and maintenance
question: Turn validated failure evidence into updates while retaining prior capabilities.

title: Socio-technical robustness and documentation
question: Preserve provenance, evaluate affected groups and privacy, and assign responsibility for deployment outcomes.
